newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: SOCCER-COLOMBIA COACH TO QUIT IF ECUADOR WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLOMBIA COACH TO QUIT IF ECUADOR WIN.

text.p: The coach of Colombia's national soccer team said he would resign if his team fails to defeat Ecuador in its World Cup qualifier next Sunday in the Caribbean port of Barranquilla.

Coach Hernan Dario Gomez -- nicknamed the "Night-stick" for his abrasive treatment of players and the press -- has been blamed for the Colombian team's growing losing streak, and began receiving death threats after the team's humiliating 4-1 loss to Chile earlier this month.
"I can't take one more loss, and neither can the Colombian people," Gomez told Colombian television at the team training grounds in Barranquilla.

Gomez did not refer specifically to the death threats, which recall for many the case of Andres Escobar, the popular Colombian defender gunned down outside a Medellin restaurant after scoring an own goal during Colombia's 1994 World Cup loss to the United States.
But he said he would be more than happy to hand over to another coach if Colombia lose on their home turf on Sunday.
After an early unbeaten run in World Cup qualifiers, Colombia have slumped to four defeats in the past five games. The team is still clinging to third place, behind Paraguay and Argentina.
But it must win Sunday to keep ahead of a chasing pack of Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Bolivia and Uruguay vying for one of four South American places in France next year.
